prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every Chicago car-accident case—“best” depends on your needs (severity of injury, whether you want to go to trial, your budget, language needs, etc.). I can, however, help you find a strong attorney by giving practical criteria, where to search, and what to ask.

Quick essentials
- Illinois personal-injury statute of limitations: normally 2 years from the accident date (735 ILCS 5/13‑202). Government claims may require much shorter notice—act promptly.
- Most car-accident PI lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Typical contingency is roughly 33% of recovery pre-suit and may be higher if the case goes to trial or appeals—read the fee agreement carefully.

How to choose the best lawyer for your case
Look for these specific qualities:
- Relevant experience: handled serious car-accident cases, experienced with your specific injury type (whiplash vs. catastrophic injury).
- Trial experience: many cases settle, but trial experience matters if the insurer won’t offer fair compensation.
- Track record of settlements/verdicts: recent results and amounts for cases similar to yours.
- Communication and availability: responsive, explains strategy in plain language.
- Resources: firm has investigators, medical experts and litigation support if needed.
- Reputation: peer ratings (Martindale‑Hubbell), Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, client reviews.
- Transparent fees and expenses: clear contingency percentage and how costs are advanced/handled.

Where to search
- Super Lawyers / Best Lawyers directories
- Avvo and Martindale‑Hubbell for ratings and client reviews
- Google Maps / Yelp for local firms and client feedback
- Illinois Trial Lawyers Association (Chicago Chapter) for experienced litigators
- Local referrals: friends, doctors, other attorneys

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many car-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?
- Have you handled cases like mine (injury type and severity)? Can you share outcomes?
- Who will handle my case—partner, associate, or staff attorney?
- What is your contingency fee and what expenses will I be responsible for?
- What’s the estimated timeline and likely value range for my case?
- How often will I get updates and by what method?

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific outcome or settlement amount
- Reluctance to put fee terms in writing
- Very high-pressure tactics to sign right away
- Poor responsiveness or avoidance of your questions

If you want, I can:
- Compile a short list of well-regarded Chicago personal-injury attorneys/firms tailored to your neighborhood and injury severity (tell me your ZIP or neighborhood, type/seriousness of injury, and any preferences like bilingual or trial-focused)
- Draft an email or phone script you can use to contact several lawyers for consultations

Which would you prefer?
